subject: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.inference.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 08:32:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up

Hi Sofia / Marcus —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re aligned on next steps and inputs we need to size Dedicated correctly: 

Summary of what we heard:
- Deployment mode: Finova is leaning toward Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools) because of steady volume and data isolation requirements.
- Models: primary models will be a larger chat/generation model (you mentioned Llama-3 34B as primary, Llama-3 13B for lower-cost paths) and an embeddings job for semantic search.
- Key SLOs: 95th percentile latency target ~400ms for chat responses under normal load; acceptable up to 800ms for bursty times.

Information we need to finalize sizing (see attached template):
1) TPS targets (steady-state and peak burst) for generation and embeddings separately
2) Average token mix: average request input tokens + average output tokens (or overall tokens per request)
3) Concurrency targets (how many simultaneous unique user requests you expect)
4) Latency SLOs and acceptable tail latency for each workload
5) Preferred GPU families (if you have procurement preferences) — if unsure, we can make recommendations based on model choices and cost targets

Proposed next steps:
- Marcus / Sofia: can you fill the attached sizing template with the numbers above?
- Marissa (SE) will review and propose a node layout (GPU type/count, instance sizing, and expected TPS/concurrency per node).
- Schedule a technical deep-dive next week to validate assumptions — I included a Cal link below; let me know what works.

Attachments: dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx (spreadsheet to capture TPS/concurrency/token mix), SOC2_packet.pdf

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.inference.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

From: Marcus Lee <mlee@enterpriseco.com>

Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up

Thanks Aditya — quick answers inline.

> 1) TPS targets (steady-state and peak burst) for generation and embeddings separately
Steady-state generation: 6 TPS (concurrent interactive users ~40)
Peak burst generation: up to 22 TPS for short windows (5-10 minutes during heavy traffic)
Embeddings: avg 40 qps for batched async jobs (can be queued), spikes to ~120 qps during nightly re-index (we can schedule)

> 2) Average token mix
Chat/generation: avg input ~130 tokens, avg output ~90 tokens (so ~220 tokens total per request)
Embeddings: 512 tokens per document average (we batch to 64/doc batch), but throughput requirement stated above

> 3) Concurrency targets
Concurrent interactive users: ~40 active writers simultaneously (each may have 1-2 inflight requests occasionally)
Background jobs: embeddings are mostly batched; concurrency for embedding model ~8 concurrent batches

> 4) Latency SLOs
Target P95 < 400ms for generation; can accept P99 up to 800ms. Embeddings can be higher (P95 < 1s) if batched.

> 5) Preferred GPU families
Procurement note: we prefer NVIDIA A100 or equivalent for production critical workloads; H100 would be great but may be cost-prohibitive. Happy for you to propose a mix (A100 for generation, A10 or A16 for embeddings).

I'm attaching our internal traffic sample (sanitized) to the HubSpot record — happy to run through it on a call.

-Marcus
VP Product Engineering, Finova AI
mlee@enterpriseco.com

Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up

Marcus — thanks for the clear numbers, this is very helpful. A few quick technical notes / recommendations based on the mix you provided: 

- Model choices: for Llama-3 34B at your latency targets, A100 80GB (or H100 if available) is our recommendation for production Dedicated nodes. Llama-3 13B can run well on smaller A10/A16 GPUs or quantized A100 slices.
- Node sizing: initial recommendation is a small pool of 3 x A100-80GB nodes for generation (gives capacity headroom for 6 TPS steady and 22 TPS burst with batching + KV cache). This also supports model variants and rolling upgrades with capacity headroom.
- Embeddings: embeddings jobs can run on separate pool of A10/A16 (2-4 nodes depending on scheduling preferences). Since embeddings can be batched and scheduled, we can start with 2 nodes and autoscale for nightly re-index spikes.
- Concurrency & batching: tune request-level concurrency to target per-GPU throughput — with our runtime you should see ~10-12 concurrent generation streams per A100 with batching and KV cache for Llama-3 34B (depends on prompt length). We'll validate with a perf run.
- Cost tradeoff: we can also propose a mixed cluster (1 H100 for peak / heavy RLHF-like requests + 2 A100s for steady) if H100 pricing is acceptable.

Next steps I can take this afternoon: fill the attached sizing template with the node-level TPS/concurrency estimates and a recommended starting configuration (GPU counts, estimated sustained TPS per pool, expected token costs). Once you confirm, we can schedule a perf validation run (30-60 minutes) to measure real TPS and latency under a representative token mix.

Questions for you: 
- Can you confirm whether the nightly re-index window is flexible (i.e., can we shift to off-peak)? That will let us use smaller embedding pools with scheduled scale-ups.
- Any hard constraints on budget that would push us to favor A10/A16 over A100?

Thanks — I’ll populate the spreadsheet and send a draft sizing shortly.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com
